dissents.topic: Severity of the _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS table design (conflating literal characters with symbolic OpenAPI names)

positions.position: P1 — the table is identity-mapping data masquerading as a mapping; conflates allowlist and translation table; the delimiter parameter complects literal characters and named OpenAPI styles
P2 — conflates two distinct concepts (literal character vs. symbolic OpenAPI style) in a single namespace; small abstraction smell that will be awkward to extend
P1 — leaky abstraction; the key set conflates characters and symbolic names with no invariant tying the two halves together; future contributor could break symmetry silently
P2 — design choice rather than a bug; fixed dict conflates OpenAPI alias translation with allow-list validation
P2 — two-level lookup table doing work a one-level mapping could do; structural cleanup, not blocking
P2 — data dominates; cleaner shape is a set of allowed chars plus a small alias dict; not blocking

dissents.topic: Whether the delimiter validation should fire consistently regardless of request shape (param-shape-dependent ValueError)

positions.position: P1 — same call with same bad argument has different behavior depending on whether the value arrived as a single string or list; validate the delimiter argument once at the top of the function
P2 — same input produces different outcomes depending on unrelated state (param present vs absent); validation of a constant-domain argument belongs at the call boundary, but not blocking
P2 — raising ValueError from a request-parsing helper conflates programmer error with request error; validate once at call time with a distinct exception type

dissents.topic: Severity of the silent no-op when delimiter is supplied but value is already a list (interaction with multiple values / auto_parse_qs_csv)

positions.position: P1 — classic LSP-style hazard; semantically identical HTTP-level inputs produce materially different results; consider applying delimiter to each element or warning when intent is unclear
P1 — specification is silent; postcondition encoded only in test, not stated in docstring; either state the postcondition explicitly or refuse the silent ignore
Not flagged as a defect — treats it as a documented invariant that simply needs a proof-by-test
Not flagged — tests cover the auto_parse_qs_csv interaction and the explode/multi-value case adequately

dissents.topic: Overload signature default style (= None vs = ...)

positions.position: P2 — small literate-programming smell; overloads overstate what they specify; align to '= ...' to match surrounding style
P1 — stylistically inconsistent with surrounding code; could confuse static analyzers checking overload compatibility

issues.description: Transform callable interaction with delimiter is not tested
issues.detail: The new split happens before the existing transform loop in get_param_as_list. The added tests do not cover delimiter combined with transform (e.g., get_param_as_list('xs', delimiter='|', transform=int)), leaving the invariant 'each returned element has been passed through transform' under-audited. Add a test to lock the contract.

issues.description: Interaction with keep_blank_qs_values is documented but not tested
issues.detail: The new docstring explicitly states that keep_blank_qs_values 'has no effect on the secondary splitting by delimiter' — a behavioral claim that 'a||b' under delimiter='|' yields ['a', '', 'b'] regardless of the option. This documented invariant is unverified by tests and easy to regress.

issues.description: delimiter argument complects literal characters and named OpenAPI styles into one parameter slot
issues.detail: The `delimiter` parameter accepts either a one-character split token (',', '|', ' ') or a symbolic style name ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited'). Two different values with two different semantics pass through the same slot, disambiguated by table lookup. A caller reading the signature cannot tell from `str | None` which kind is expected. Separating them (e.g., `delimiter` for literal and `style` for named style) would make the value simple instead of overloaded.

issues.description: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS table is identity-mapping data masquerading as a mapping (allowlist conflated with translation)
issues.detail: Three of the five entries map a character to itself; the other two map a name to a character. The dict is both an allowlist and a translation table at once. A simpler decomposition is a set of allowed delimiter characters plus a tiny alias map ({'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}). No invariant ties the symbolic and literal halves together, so a future contributor could add 'tabDelimited' -> '\t' without adding '\t' as a key and break symmetry silently.

issues.description: Overload signatures use `= None` where the file convention is `= ...` (Ellipsis) for overload defaults
issues.detail: All six @overload signatures declare 'delimiter: str | None = None' as a concrete default, but every other parameter in those overloads uses `= ...` as the placeholder default. Mixing literal `= None` into overloads is stylistically inconsistent with the surrounding code and could confuse static analyzers that check overload compatibility. Use `= ...` in overloads and keep `= None` only on the implementation.

issues.description: Delimiter validation only fires when the param is a single string, producing inconsistent behavior across request shapes
issues.detail: The validation `if delimiter not in _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS: raise ValueError(...)` is nested inside `if delimiter is not None and isinstance(items, str)`. Calling `get_param_as_list('x', delimiter=';')` raises when the value is a single string but silently accepts the bogus delimiter when the param appeared multiple times or was already CSV-split. Same call, same bad argument, different behavior depending on the request shape. Validate the delimiter argument once at the top of the function.

issues.description: Contract for `delimiter` is ambiguous: typed as `str | None` but only five string values are accepted
issues.detail: The signature declares `delimiter: str | None`, but the contract actually accepts only five strings (',', '|', ' ', 'pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited'). The type system is being used as decoration rather than specification — a Literal type listing the five accepted values would let mypy reject bad call sites at static-check time. Either narrow to `Literal[...] | None` or expose the constants as named symbols (Enum or module-level constants) so callers can program against the contract rather than magic strings.

issues.description: Silent contract divergence: `delimiter` is ignored when the value is already a list (multi-value or auto_parse_qs_csv path)
issues.detail: When the same query parameter appears multiple times (explode style) or has already been split by `auto_parse_qs_csv`, `delimiter` becomes a no-op because `isinstance(items, str)` is false. Two callers passing semantically identical inputs at the HTTP level (`?phrase=a%20b&phrase=c` vs `?phrase=a%20b,c` with csv on) get materially different results from the same call. The docstring mentions this only as a Note; the postcondition belongs in the formal contract, or the behavior should be changed (e.g., apply delimiter to each element, or warn).

issues.description: Error message leaks dict insertion order into the public contract
issues.detail: The ValueError reports `tuple(_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS)` — a tuple whose order is the dict's insertion order. This is observable, untested, and unspecified, exactly the kind of incidental property that becomes load-bearing once someone writes a test against the message text. Sort the keys or partition them into characters and symbolic names with a stable presentation.

issues.description: Delimiter allowlist rejects legitimate single-character delimiters like ';' or '\t'
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS is a closed set of five entries. A caller passing delimiter=';' gets ValueError (codified by the test). The fixed dict conflates OpenAPI alias translation with allow-list validation; a cleaner factoring is a small alias dict plus a 'must be a single character' rule, which would keep the OpenAPI convenience without forbidding semicolons in user code.

issues.description: Raising ValueError from a request-parsing helper conflates programmer error with request error
issues.detail: `get_param_as_list` is documented to raise `HTTPBadRequest` for bad request data and to convert transform `ValueError` into `HTTPBadRequest`. A bad `delimiter` argument is a programmer error, not a request error, but it surfaces as a bare `ValueError` inside a request handler — precisely the kind of exception Falcon usually channels into a 500. Validate `delimiter` at call/decoration time and use a distinct exception type to separate the two failure modes.

issues.description: Allowlist policy is fused into the same function as the split itself
issues.detail: Splitting a string on a delimiter is a pure, general operation; restricting it to three characters is a policy. The policy is reasonable (matches OpenAPI) but is fused into the same function. If a user later needs ';' they must monkey-patch the module-level dict or stop using this API. Pushing the allowlist to the edge (thin wrapper) while the core split is just `value.split(char)` would keep the value-transforming core simple.

issues.description: Empty-string, blank, and trailing/whitespace token edge cases are not exercised by tests
issues.detail: The docstring calls out that `keep_blank_qs_values` does not affect the secondary split, but no test verifies what `get_param_as_list('x', delimiter=',')` returns when the value is `''`, `'a,,b'`, `'a, b'`, `'names=a,b,'`, or `'Luke,'`. Python's str.split returns ['' ], ['Luke'], ['Luke', '' ] respectively. For a feature whose entire job is splitting strings, these corner cases of empty tokens, trailing delimiters, and whitespace are exactly what the next maintainer will want pinned by regression test.

issues.description: Docstring Raises section not updated for new ValueError failure mode
issues.detail: The method's docstring lists `HTTPBadRequest` under Raises but does not document the new `ValueError` raised when an unsupported delimiter is passed. Every observable postcondition — including raised exceptions — belongs in the spec; a caller cannot learn the precondition on `delimiter` without reading the implementation.

issues.description: Six @overload signatures grew solely to thread one optional kwarg through
issues.detail: Each of the six get_param_as_list overloads grew a `delimiter: str | None = None` line. This is a Python typing constraint, not a design smell of this PR per se, but the overload set is now carrying real maintenance weight; any future kwarg multiplies it again. A signal that the signature is fighting the dispatch. Not blocking.

issues.description: Complexity and allocation are fine but worth stating explicitly
issues.detail: The added work is one dict lookup plus a single str.split — O(n) in the value length, one allocation, obvious termination. No hidden quadratic, no regex. Stating this explicitly so the rigor is in the record rather than implied.

issues.description: Control flow trivial but the surrounding function is approaching reader-cognitive-limit
issues.detail: The added block is a straight selection followed by an assignment — no smuggled goto, no flag. Termination is trivial. However, the rest of get_param_as_list has accreted enough conditional branching that a future addition of 'just one more case' would push the function past the threshold where a reader can hold the control flow in their head. Worth watching.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the change is small, well-scoped, and algorithmically sound: a dict lookup plus one str.split with no hidden complexity. The strongest convergent concern is contract clarity at the boundary — five out of six reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Torvalds, Liskov, Pike, Dijkstra) independently flag that _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS conflates a literal-character allowlist with an OpenAPI symbolic-name translation table, though they split on severity (Hickey and Dijkstra call it P1; Knuth, Torvalds, Liskov, and Pike call it P2). The second convergent finding (Torvalds, Pike, Hickey) is that delimiter validation only fires when the param happens to be a single string, so the same bad argument silently passes or raises depending on request shape. The strongest preserved disagreement is on the silent no-op when the value is already a list: Liskov and Dijkstra call this a P1 LSP/spec hazard requiring docstring change or behavioral fix, while Knuth and Pike treat it as documented behavior that merely needs more tests. Test coverage gaps (transform interaction, keep_blank_qs_values, empty/trailing-delimiter cases) are flagged by multiple reviewers as the most concrete pre-merge ask.
